content:
Following the release of the seventh developer betas for iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and Apple's other upcoming software updates, Apple is now rolling out the corresponding public betas. Here's everything you need to know.

Apple Releases New Public Betas

Earlier today, Apple released:

  • iOS 27 developer beta 7 (build number: 24A5424a)
  • iPadOS 27 developer beta 7 (build number: 24A5424a)
  • macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 7 (build number: 26A5421a)
  • tvOS 27 developer beta 7 (build number: 24J5358a)
  • visionOS 27 developer beta 7 (build number: 24M5359a)
  • watchOS 27 developer beta 7 (build number: 24R5358a)

Apple is now making the corresponding builds available to public beta testers, marking the fifth public beta release. So far, Apple has rolled out new public betas for iOS 27, tvOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and HomePod 27.

Today's builds don't include any particularly notable changes, as Apple is now primarily focused on bug fixes and stability improvements ahead of the official release in a few weeks.

Additionally, after releasing the corresponding developer release candidates earlier this morning, Apple has also rolled out the second public release candidate of macOS Sequoia 15.8 (24H20). The second public release candidate of macOS Tahoe 26.7 (25G224) is expected to arrive shortly. (Available as of 7:42 PM ET.)

Across all of today's releases, the public beta build numbers match their developer counterparts.

Sign Up for the Apple Public Beta Program

If you'd like to register your device for the public beta program, visit https://beta.apple.com and follow the steps for each respective device. Here's how to install the public beta on iPhone:

  • Visit the Apple Beta Software Program website, then choose Sign Up or Sign In.
  • Sign in with the same Apple Account you use on your iPhone. Then accept the program terms and enroll your account.
  • Open Settings on your iPhone.
  • Go to General > Software Update > Beta Updates.
  • Select iOS 27 Public Beta.
  • Return to the Software Update screen, then tap Update Now when the beta appears.

Apple recommends installing beta software on a secondary device. If you're using your primary iPhone, make sure to back it up recently first.

Have you spotted any changes in today's betas? Let us know in the comments.
